world_rules: At night the shop is locked; the cashier serves through a night pay drawer in the glass and never opens the door — a rule for a woman working alone.
There is a panic button under the counter; pressing it calls it in and cannot be taken back.
Jo cannot know whether the man at the hatch is a victim in trouble or a danger to her; the night gives her no way to find out.
Jo's son Kieran has been in and out of trouble for years and she does not hear from him; every man in trouble at a window at night is, to her, somebody's boy.
locations: the kiosk, behind the night glass
the forecourt, on the man's side of the glass
objects: the night pay drawer in the glass
the panic button under the counter
the key to the outside toilet, round the back, out of the cameras
